longs.thesis: Q3 blowout — revenue $5.83B (+83% y/y), adjusted EPS $3.30 beating consensus ~$2.93-3.02; 2026 revenue raised to $21B and a first-ever 2027 target of $40B on AI infrastructure demand. Violent bounce off the 52-week low after Monday's -5% drop; earnings call 8:00 AM ET today.

M&A — Ares Capital agreed to buy MidCap Financial in a ~$2.6B stock-and-cash deal at $10.88/share (~30% premium to Monday's $8.36 close: ~$1.21 cash + ~$9.67 ARCC stock). Premarket price still below the deal price, pricing in deal risk/closing time.

Results released a day early — a wider Q3 loss, but a stronger Q4 unit-revenue outlook and further operating-margin improvement, lifting it off record/all-time lows after a -19% five-day slide. Beaten-down reversal attempt.

Reported M&A — DoorDash in advanced/exclusive talks to acquire Instacart for ~$17B, possibly announced as soon as this week. Monday's +7.9% to $60.88 was already the M&A repricing; follow-through above Monday's high is the continuation trigger.

shorts.thesis: Q3 disaster — adjusted loss of $0.21/share vs ~$1.04 profit expected, revenue $3.68B (-8.8% y/y) vs ~$3.92-3.97B expected, North America operating profit -44.7%, and the third guidance cut of 2026. Breakdown continuation in a long-term downtrend, already -63% year-to-date.

Q3 pretax profit $9.63B (+32% y/y) still missed expectations, revenue $18.62B vs $19.16B expected, and the new $1B buyback did not offset margin/windfall-tax worries into the UK budget. Large-cap bank gap-down on an earnings miss.

shorts.exit_reason: Stop hit — day high 1.76 >= stop 1.65. (stop-before-target convention; target 1.3 also touched at day low 1.2901).
shorts.thesis: Reversal side of Monday's +97.17% session-leading surge with no fresh catalyst confirmed — a parabolic one-day spike giving back ground premarket. Chasing either direction without a fresh catalyst is the risk.
